pointers.sentence: Under ASGI the method's asynchronous twin makes the same call (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`).

Of what comes back the handler checks little: `BaseHandler.check_response` refuses `None` and a coroutine nobody awaited, and tests nothing else ([What the handler asks of a view](views/callable.md)) (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler.check_response`).

`render` renders a template into a finished response, `redirect` makes a redirect to a URL, to a pattern's name reversed or to an object's own URL, and `get_object_or_404` fetches one object, raising `Http404` when there is none ([The shortcuts](views/shortcuts.md)) (`django/shortcuts.py`).

Each time that function is called it makes a new instance of the class, stores the request and its arguments on it in `View.setup`, and calls the instance's `dispatch` (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.as_view`).

A request whose method is not in `View.http_method_names`, or for which the instance has no method of that name, is answered with a 405 listing the methods it does answer (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).

A request whose method is not in `View.http_method_names`, or for which the instance has no method of that name, is answered with a 405 listing the methods it does answer (`django/views/generic/base.py:View.dispatch`, `django/views/generic/base.py:View.http_method_not_allowed`).

`require_GET`, outermost on the masthead, answers a `"POST"` with a 405, and neither the other two wrappers nor the view runs ([View decorators](views/decorators.md)) (`django/views/decorators/http.py:require_http_methods`).

`csrf_exempt` returns a wrapper that only calls the view, with an attribute set on it: a **mark**, which `CsrfViewMiddleware` reads when the handler shows it the view (`django/views/decorators/csrf.py:csrf_exempt`).

Others are a middleware class applied to one view: `csrf_protect` and `cache_page` each make an instance of their middleware, `CsrfViewMiddleware` or `CacheMiddleware`, for the view they decorate, and a wrapper that calls its hooks around the view ([A middleware as a decorator](views/middleware-decorators.md)) (`django/utils/decorators.py:make_middleware_decorator`).

It applies the decorator anew at every call, so a decorator made from a middleware class makes a middleware for every request ([Decorating a class: `method_decorator`](views/method-decorator.md)) (`django/utils/decorators.py:method_decorator`).

ArticleDetail names a model and inherits everything else from `DetailView`, whose `get` is a handler method with its decisions taken out and made methods of their own: `get_object` finds the article from the slug the path captured, `get_context_data` builds the template's context, and `render_to_response` makes the response, with a template name made from the app's label and the model's name when the class names none (`django/views/generic/detail.py:BaseDetailView.get`).

For each of the four statuses it may choose, 404, 500, 400 and 403, it has an **error view**: the one the URLconf names (`handler404` and its three kin), or else Django's default from `django/views/defaults.py`, called with the request and, for every status but 500, the exception ([The error views](views/errors.md)).

With `settings.DEBUG` on, an `Http404`, an exception the handler does not recognise, and a `BadRequest` or `SuspiciousOperation` are answered with a **debug page** instead, while a `PermissionDenied` still goes to its error view (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

The same reporter writes the report that `AdminEmailHandler` mails to a site's administrators ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](views/debug.md)) (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter`, `django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.emit`).

The same reporter writes the report that `AdminEmailHandler` mails to a site's administrators ([The debug pages and `ExceptionReporter`](views/debug.md)) (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter`, `django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.emit`).

`django.views.static.serve` answers a request with a file from a directory; `django.conf.urls.static.static` routes a prefix to it only while `settings.DEBUG` is on, and the static files app's own view calls it ([The static file view](views/static-files.md)) (`django/views/static.py:serve`).
